attrs.evidence: lowering_check.mjs 13/13, the first end-to-end witness: add(const 2, const 3) with inputs={} lowers to one canonical ic32 term whose identity the kernel and ic32_canon agree on; the host launches the catalogued binary and observes the canonical normal form L0(L1(A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,N1))))))); that decodes structurally to {status:'value', value:5}; and its outcome id EQUALS the source evaluator's, whose result was itself accepted by an authority owning every oracle it consulted (derivation.acceptance-authority@1). six-identities-stay-distinct asserts all six values differ. native-film-absent-by-refusal asserts the film emitter REFUSES this exact fixture with film-dup-cell-present — the gap is measured at the fixture the refinement runs on rather than described in the abstract. At B1.2.1 the anti-collapse case is chain-identities-stay-distinct: it requires a value for every node REFINEMENT_CHAIN marks exercised, fails if a declared node is not wired into the witness, and NAMES the unexercised ones in its output -- a node silently absent and a node declared absent being the difference between a stale instrument and a scoped one. B2: every node of REFINEMENT_CHAIN is now exercised -- the witness reaches native code THROUGH instantiate(), so instantiation_sem_id and inputs_sem_id stopped being declared architecture.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B2.1 and kept as history. Revision 3 described instantiation as a single relation that both substituted and emitted, and permitted a rule vocabulary of bare names. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED BY THE ASSURANCE MACHINERY -- but revision 3 did permit a real compiler-layer defect, the two-read input binding, which is recorded in the successor rather than here because the successor is where it is fixed.
attrs.statement: SOURCE AND TARGET AGREE ON THE OUTCOME: source_outcome_sem_id == target_outcome_sem_id, where the target side is reached by canonical lowering, native ic32 execution, and structural decoding. TWO GRADES OF EVIDENCE FOR THE EXECUTION LEG, and only the first is claimed here. OBSERVED: the ObservedExecutionHost hashed a catalogued binary and then ran it, so the normal form is an execution event the host drove (derivation.implementation-provenance@4). FILM-EVIDENCED: the transition sequence itself is replayed by the independent kernel (film.native-emission@1). BOTH ARE NOW CLAIMED for the first witness: ic32_film v0.2.0 emits six chained APP-LAM frames for the lowered term and the kernel replays the chain. Round 25 recorded the second as OPEN on the strength of a refusal that was right about the fixture and wrong about its reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires none. What remains OPEN is a fixture where a DUP-* rule actually becomes enabled. Reporting the two grades separately is the point: an execution the host observed and an execution the kernel replayed are different claims. THIS IS THE THEOREM; canonical-lowering@1 and target-decoding@1 exist to make it DIAGNOSABLE, because a bare equality failure cannot say which of three relations broke. THE CHAIN'S IDENTITIES STAY DISTINCT AND NONE MAY BE COLLAPSED INTO ANOTHER, and the chain is DECLARED rather than counted in prose: program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id, target_nf_sem_id, decode_sem_id, outcome_sem_id, of which the last two of the first five are DECLARED AND NOT EXERCISED until instantiation is built. THIS SENTENCE SAID 'SIX' AND OMITTED target_template_sem_id for the whole of B1.2, the pass that introduced it as an independently identified semantic object -- so the law, and the anti-collapse witness reading it, made a six-way claim about a seven-node chain and were green throughout. The enumeration now lives in REFINEMENT_CHAIN with an exercised flag per node and the witness DERIVES its set from it, because a hand-typed count drifting from the thing it counts is a species this tree has now caught in a law count, a case count, a rung count and here. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. THE SOURCE-TO-TEMPLATE MAP IS STRUCTURAL AND INTERPRETED: lower() reads op_lowering_rules rather than carrying a second hand-coded copy of it, so a rule cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving LOWERING_SEM_ID. English rules beside a hand-coded implementation are two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed -- the codomain-in-prose defect one layer in -- and `transform: identity` on the port's source name is the no-normalization ruling made structural rather than stated. LOWER() NO LONGER RETURNS AN EXECUTABLE TERM. The convenience field was a SECOND PATH: the official route through instantiate() beside a shortcut through lowering, with every future reader having to remember which carried the semantics, which is how a hidden second mechanism returns. It is removed and the equality survives as a REGRESSION THEOREM -- instantiate(template, {}) reproduces the exact 129 bytes, the same six-frame film, the same normal form and the same 5. AND instantiate() MAY NOT MINT THE IDENTITY OF ITS OWN OUTPUT: an instantiator that emitted bytes and certified their semantic id would produce the artifact and the certificate from one source, so a wrong emission would carry a matching id and verify against itself. The kernel canonicalises the bytes; the receipt is built around that id; verification RE-INSTANTIATES and RE-CANONICALISES independently rather than asking the instantiator to agree with itself. THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER MOVED TO STATUS and gained two conditions: split emission into its own relation when it becomes independently REUSED, independently THEOREM-BEARING, independently VERSIONED OR REPLACEABLE, or when the closed-template intermediate becomes an independently IDENTIFIED or EXTERNALLY OBSERVED artifact. The last two fire first -- the moment two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong. Keeping that trigger inside the hashed semantics, as B1.2.1 did, re-committed B1.1's own finding: governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when it is reworded. STILL DECLARED OPEN: source-refusal to instantiation-refusal preservation, unchanged.
